rs-rb-why.back: To mark: antlers and forehead glands leave a visual sign and scent. Glands are most active in autumn.
rs-rb-why.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="A buck rubs his antlers and forehead on a sapling. Glands on his forehead leave scent on the bare wood, so a rub is both a visual sign and a scent post.">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="300" rx="0" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="200" y="28" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Why bucks rub</text>
<rect x="261.0" y="60" width="18" height="200" rx="2" fill="#6b4f35"/><rect x="261.0" y="120" width="18" height="80" rx="2" fill="#f4e3b5"/><path d="M255.0 206 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M255.0 210 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M255.0 214 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><g transform="translate(170 262) scale(1.6)" fill="#8b5a2b"><path d="M-35 -40 Q-10 -48 20 -42 L28 -58 L34 -66 L44 -64 L42 -56 L48 -50 L36 -46 L32 -34 Q30 -26 26 -24 L28 0 L23 0 L20 -22 Q0 -20 -20 -24 L-22 0 L-27 0 L-29 -26 Q-38 -30 -35 -40 Z"/><path d="M34 -66 L30 -76 M38 -66 L42 -78" stroke="#6b4f35" stroke-width="2.5" fill="none"/></g><circle cx="240" cy="154" r="7" fill="#e8590c"/><text x="150" y="92" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="middle">forehead glands</text><line x1="200" y1="98" x2="236" y2="148" stroke="#e8590c" stroke-width="2"/><text x="330" y="120" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">scent</text><text x="330" y="138" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">left on</text><text x="330" y="156" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">the wood</text><text x="200" y="290" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">A rub is a sign and a scent post (70%)</text>
</svg>

rs-rb-age.back: Yes. Rubbing tracks testosterone; yearlings make about half as many rubs as prime age bucks.

rs-rb-height.front: Rub height that suggests a mature buck?
rs-rb-height.back: Centred 75 cm or higher (60%). Most rubs are 30 to 105 cm.
rs-rb-height.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Step 1: measure how high the rub goes from the ground. A rub centred 75 centimetres or higher suggests a mature buck.">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="300" rx="0" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="200" y="28" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">1. Height</text>
<rect x="192.0" y="50" width="16" height="210" rx="2" fill="#6b4f35"/><rect x="192.0" y="155" width="16" height="60" rx="2" fill="#f4e3b5"/><path d="M186.0 221 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M186.0 225 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M186.0 229 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="240" y1="260" x2="240" y2="155" stroke="#e8590c" stroke-width="3"/><text x="300" y="210" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="middle">top of rub</text><text x="300" y="230" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="middle">from ground</text><rect x="0" y="260" width="400" height="40" rx="0" fill="#cfdcb5"/><text x="110" y="160" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">75 cm or more:</text><text x="110" y="180" font-size="15" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">maybe mature (60%)</text>
</svg>

rs-rb-tree.back: 2.5 to 5 cm often young bucks; over 10 cm usually older. Height is the better clue.
rs-rb-tree.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 306" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Step 2: measure the tree diameter. Trees 2.5 to 5 centimetres are often rubbed by young bucks; over 10 centimetres usually older bucks. Height matters more than tree size.">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="306" rx="0" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="200" y="28" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">2. Tree size</text>
<rect x="170" y="60" width="60" height="200" rx="4" fill="#6b4f35"/><rect x="170" y="120" width="60" height="80" rx="4" fill="#f4e3b5"/><line x1="170" y1="270" x2="230" y2="270" stroke="#e8590c" stroke-width="3"/><text x="240" y="275" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="start">diameter</text><text x="320" y="110" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">2.5 to 5 cm:</text><text x="320" y="130" font-size="15" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">often young</text><text x="320" y="170" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">over 10 cm:</text><text x="320" y="190" font-size="15" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">often older</text><text x="200" y="296" font-size="15" fill="#6b4f35" text-anchor="middle">Height beats tree size (60%)</text>
</svg>

rs-rb-fresh.back: Wet bright wood, curled shavings below, sap. Old: grey and dry.
rs-rb-fresh.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Step 3: age it. A fresh rub has bright wet wood, curled bark shavings on the ground and sap. An old rub is grey and dry.">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="300" rx="0" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="200" y="28" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">3. Fresh or old?</text>
<rect x="60" y="70" width="120" height="180" rx="10" fill="#fff" stroke="#dfe6d3" stroke-width="1.5"/><rect x="111.0" y="80" width="18" height="150" rx="2" fill="#6b4f35"/><rect x="111.0" y="120" width="18" height="70" rx="2" fill="#f4e3b5"/><path d="M105.0 196 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M105.0 200 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M105.0 204 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><text x="120" y="268" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="middle">Fresh</text><rect x="220" y="70" width="120" height="180" rx="10" fill="#fff" stroke="#dfe6d3" stroke-width="1.5"/><rect x="271.0" y="80" width="18" height="150" rx="2" fill="#6b4f35"/><rect x="271.0" y="120" width="18" height="70" rx="2" fill="#b8ad97"/><path d="M265.0 196 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#b8ad97" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M265.0 200 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#b8ad97" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M265.0 204 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#b8ad97" stroke-width="2"/><text x="280" y="268" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#8a9a6b" text-anchor="middle">Old</text><text x="120" y="290" font-size="14" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">wet, curls, sap</text><text x="280" y="290" font-size="14" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">grey, dry</text>
</svg>

rs-rb-side.front: Which way did the buck come from?
rs-rb-side.back: The side that is rubbed usually faces where he came from.
rs-rb-side.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 296" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Step 4: note which side is rubbed. The rubbed side usually faces the direction the buck came from, so a line of rubs shows his route.">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="296" rx="0" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="200" y="28" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">4. Which side?</text>
<rect x="190.0" y="70" width="20" height="170" rx="2" fill="#6b4f35"/><rect x="190.0" y="120" width="20" height="70" rx="2" fill="#f4e3b5"/><path d="M184.0 196 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M184.0 200 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M184.0 204 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="60" y1="200" x2="180" y2="200" stroke="#e8590c" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M180.0 200.0 L171.0 204.3 L171.0 195.7 Z" fill="#e8590c"/><text x="90" y="186" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="middle">buck came</text><text x="90" y="226" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="middle">from here</text><text x="310" y="150" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">rubbed side</text><text x="310" y="170" font-size="15" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">faces back</text><text x="310" y="190" font-size="15" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">along his path</text><text x="200" y="284" font-size="15" fill="#6b4f35" text-anchor="middle">Rub lines show his route (60%)</text>
</svg>

rs-rb-line.back: Rubs in a row facing one way: his route between bed and feed.

rs-rb-signpost.back: A big tree rubbed year after year, kept up mostly by mature bucks.
rs-rb-signpost.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="A signpost rub: a big tree rubbed year after year, mostly kept going by mature bucks. Younger bucks and does may visit it.">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="300" rx="0" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="200" y="28" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Signpost rubs</text>
<rect x="183.0" y="50" width="34" height="210" rx="2" fill="#6b4f35"/><rect x="183.0" y="110" width="34" height="120" rx="2" fill="#f4e3b5"/><path d="M177.0 236 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M177.0 240 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M177.0 244 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="0" y="260" width="400" height="40" rx="0" fill="#cfdcb5"/><text x="80" y="110" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">big tree</text><text x="80" y="130" font-size="15" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">rubbed</text><text x="80" y="150" font-size="15" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">year after</text><text x="80" y="170" font-size="15" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">year</text><text x="320" y="110" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">mature</text><text x="320" y="130" font-size="15" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">bucks</text><text x="320" y="150" font-size="15" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">keep it</text><text x="320" y="170" font-size="15" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">going (60%)</text>
</svg>

rs-rb-mule.back: Fewer rubs, on small conifers and shrubs. Mule deer rarely scrape.

rs-rb-elk.front: Bark stripped above your head on a big tree?
rs-rb-elk.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Rub height by species. Deer: knee to waist high on small trees. Elk: big trees stripped up to over your head. Moose: thrash and strip willow and alder, rub saplings.">

<text x="200" y="28" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Whose rub is it?</text>

</svg>

rs-rb-moose.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Rub height by species. Deer: knee to waist high on small trees. Elk: big trees stripped up to over your head. Moose: thrash and strip willow and alder, rub saplings.">

<text x="200" y="28" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Whose rub is it?</text>
<rect x="0" y="262" width="400" height="38" rx="0" fill="#cfdcb5"/><rect x="75.0" y="72" width="10" height="190" rx="2" fill="#6b4f35"/><rect x="75.0" y="157" width="10" height="75" rx="2" fill="#f4e3b5"/><path d="M69.0 238 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M69.0 242 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M69.0 246 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><text x="80" y="62" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Deer</text><rect x="189.0" y="72" width="22" height="190" rx="2" fill="#6b4f35"/><rect x="189.0" y="62" width="22" height="170" rx="2" fill="#f4e3b5"/><path d="M183.0 238 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M183.0 242 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M183.0 246 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><text x="200" y="62" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Elk</text><rect x="312.0" y="72" width="16" height="190" rx="2" fill="#6b4f35"/><rect x="312.0" y="102" width="16" height="130" rx="2" fill="#f4e3b5"/><path d="M306.0 238 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M306.0 242 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M306.0 246 q4 -6 8 0" fill="none" stroke="#f4e3b5" stroke-width="2"/><text x="320" y="62" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Moose</text><line x1="20" y1="157" x2="380" y2="157" stroke="#c9c9b9" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/><text x="380" y="150" font-size="14" fill="#6b4f35" text-anchor="end">~1 m</text><text x="80" y="290" font-size="14" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">knee to waist</text><text x="200" y="290" font-size="14" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">over your head</text><text x="320" y="290" font-size="14" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">thrashed brush</text>
</svg>

rs-sc-what.back: A pawed bare oval of soil, soaked with urine, under a licking branch about 1.2 to 1.5 m up.
rs-sc-what.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Scrape anatomy: an oval of pawed bare soil soaked with urine under an overhanging licking branch about 1.2 to 1.5 metres up. The buck chews the branch tip and rubs it with glands on his face.">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="300" rx="0" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="200" y="28" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">A scrape, side view</text>
<rect x="0" y="240" width="400" height="60" rx="0" fill="#cfdcb5"/><rect x="330" y="40" width="20" height="220" rx="3" fill="#6b4f35"/><path d="M340 80 Q250 70 150 110" fill="none" stroke="#6b4f35" stroke-width="6"/><path d="M150 110 l-14 6 M170 104 l-10 10 M190 98 l-8 12" fill="none" stroke="#6b4f35" stroke-width="3"/><ellipse cx="160" cy="250" rx="70" ry="14" fill="#5c4532"/><text x="160" y="285" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">pawed bare soil, urine</text><line x1="80" y1="110" x2="80" y2="240" stroke="#e8590c" stroke-width="2"/><text x="70" y="170" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="end">1.2 to</text><text x="70" y="188" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="end">1.5 m</text><text x="210" y="66" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">licking branch: chewed, rubbed</text>
</svg>

rs-sc-lick.front: What does a buck do to the licking branch?
rs-sc-lick.back: Chews it and rubs it with the preorbital gland near his eye.

The buck chews the branch tip and rubs it with glands on his face.">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="300" rx="0" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="200" y="28" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">A scrape, side view</text>

</svg>

rs-sc-when.back: About 80% from mid October to mid November (northern deer).
rs-sc-when.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 290" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Timeline from August to December. Velvet comes off in late August and September, rubbing runs September to November, scraping peaks from mid October to mid November, and the rut and breeding follow in November. Bars are approximate.">

rs-sc-where.front: Which scrapes get more daylight visits?
rs-sc-where.back: Those close to bedding cover (Tip). Field edge scrapes are mostly night.

rs-sc-wireless.front: Wireless trail camera for hunting in BC in October?
rs-sc-wireless.back: Unlawful from 1 August to 10 December (Region 1 all year). A memory card camera is not wireless.

rs-sc-urine.front: Store bought deer urine lure in BC?
rs-sc-urine.back: No. Cervid parts or derivatives from outside BC are banned for hunting; urine can carry CWD.

rs-rb-lean.front: Beginner lean for rubs and scrapes?
rs-rb-lean.back: Ambush a fresh rub line near the cover end at first and last light, wind in your face.
